title: Minimax Estimation of Dilation Policy Effects for Functional Gaussian Treatments near Identity
banked_reason: Sound matching risk and honest-length dilation frontier, but D0.5.G tier=subfield below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4 and not salvageable within fixed known-law scope.
gap_reasons: Its scope remains the fixed known Gaussian spectrum, complete treatment observation, and scalar dilation; it establishes neither unknown-law inference nor reconstructed-curve guarantees.

The transport computation establishes accuracy and termination through growing grids and finite optimization, without establishing feasible runtime at useful tolerances or demonstrating calibration numerically.
The projected score is constrained by the narrow benchmark, conservative inference, and absence of delivered computational evidence connecting the exact-bias theorem to usable confidence widths.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived matching minimax squared-risk and finite-sample honest interval-length orders across small-dilation and logarithmic regimes, including exact identity cancellation; strengthened the response range to [0,1] and certified the exact prefix-bias transport profile. Math and decision panels passed without findings after five cited-source attestations, but the final cold review assessed subfield (score ceiling 7.3), below the standing field floor; an independent validity gate confirmed no bounded in-scope repair. Stopped before F1, so no Lean proof was attempted; the non-load-bearing fixed-size scalar representation question and practical runtime/calibration remain unresolved.
tldr: For a known Gaussian treatment in \(\ell^2\), multiplying every coordinate by \(1+\delta\) produces a singular policy law for every \(\delta>0\). Over the full class of globally one-Lipschitz Bernoulli means \(m:H\to[0,1]\), the causal contrast has uniform minimax squared risk \(r(n,\delta)=\delta^2/\sqrt n+\delta^4/\log(e+n\delta^4)\) and honest expected interval length of order \(\sqrt{r(n,\delta)}\). Centered finite-coordinate weights, a public cutoff, projection, and a public bias allowance attain both orders. Interior Bernoulli radial alternatives give all-procedure converses that transfer to this full class. The transition is \(n\delta^4=1\), and the minimax risk and length are exactly zero at identity. The certified sharp-approximation theorem also characterizes and evaluates the exact finite-coordinate bias profile through bounded-cost transport and finite linear programs; the simpler \(\delta/\sqrt k\) allowance remains rate-optimal.
gap: Functional-policy inference under bounded finite-score ratios and generic off-policy modulus theory do not evaluate the signed all-mode Gaussian dilation contrast over the full bounded Lipschitz class uniformly at identity.
fill: An evaluated two-parameter rate, a public coordinate cutoff, one estimator and finite-sample honest connected interval, and full-observation Bernoulli converses resolve the proposed transition. A separate transport question refines the public approximation allowance.
